full: Why do prices end in 99, not a round number? Only a cent less and the first digit drops. In studies, $2.99 felt smaller than 3. But $3.59 versus $3.60, no effect, same first digit. In field tests, nine endings lifted demand, most for new items. So use a 9 where it flips the first digit. For feel-good purchases, a round price can feel right. Follow Warbans to decode how brands sell.
